_comment: Layoff / instability risk signals. `companies` is matched (case-insensitive substring) against the posting company at load time; the highest-matching entry wins. `keywords_high` / `keywords_medium` are matched against the report text + tracker notes (fixed-term, backfill, restructuring…) so a risky *posting* is flagged even at a healthy company. The dashboard shows a badge and offers a 'hide high-risk' filter. Extend freely — this is your layoff-aversion thesis made into data. Sources should be datestamped so stale flags can be pruned.

Alfen.reason: 2024 profit warnings + sharp stock decline; cost-cutting / reorganisation reported

Nyrstar.reason: European zinc-smelter curtailments due to energy costs; production halts

NET-A-PORTER.reason: YNAP sold by Richemont into Mytheresa/LuxExperience — merger integration + layoff risk

YOOX.reason: Part of YNAP — same distressed merger integration risk

Sandisk.reason: Recent Western Digital spin-off; cyclical memory market

Ruby Labs.reason: Contractor-model subscription apps; volatile, no employment stability

_keywords_note: high = unambiguous employment-instability phrasing only. Words like 'restructuring'/'reorganisation'/'turnaround' were intentionally REMOVED because in data-role JDs they usually mean *data* restructuring, not company layoffs — they mislabelled healthy employers (e.g. Adyen). Keep this list precise.
